NIPC #74-228
Illinois Department of
Transportation
Lincoln Highway Widening
Relationship to Comprehensive Regional Planning
The proposed project consists of reconstructing F.A.P. 23 (Lincoln Highway) from the present two (2) ten foot lanes in each direction to three (3) twelve foot lanes in each direction between Cicero Avenue in Matteson to Western Avenue and two (2) twelve foot lanes in each direction between Western Avenue and Chicago Road (Dixie Highway) in Chicago Heights. A sixteen foot median is included which is generally mountable with the exception of the section between Olympian Way and Brookwood Drive which is non-mountable. Also included is a separate storm sewer system and the replacement of eight (8) structures including the I.C.G. Railroad underpass.
F.A.P. 23 (Lincoln Highway) is designated as an arterial highway in the Highway Interim Plan of the Regional Transportation Plan and Program. In 1970, the average daily traffic on F.A.P. 23 (Lincoln Highway) varied from 9,565 to 20,475 vehicles per day within the project limits. Based on the Chicago Area Transportation Study's assignments, the projected traffic for the year 1990 on Lincoln Highway varies from 23,800 to 32,000 vehicles per day. These traffic volumes would justify the proposed improvements.
While some additional right-of-way will be required along the project length, the only possible conflict appears in the vicinity of the Roosevelt Elementary School in Chicago Heights. The Illinois Department of Transportation has made efforts to compensate the Roosevelt School for the acquisition of right-of-way in terms of land replacement by closing a portion of Sunnyside Avenue and a monetary settlement which would be negotiated between the City of Chicago Heights and IDOT.
It is also recommended that the improvement of Lincoln Highway in the vicinity of the Illinois Central Railroad be coordinated with the proposed reconstruction and improvement of the 21lth street commuter station (NIPC #73-170).
The project is found to be consistent with regional planning policies as set forth in the <u>Comprehensive General Plan</u> and with currently adopted Commission plans and programs.
